records.literal_gloss: He said then to the disciples of him, Impossible it is for the stumbling blocks not to come, but woe [to him] through whom they come;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, but woe [to the one] through whom they come!
en.B: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Things that trip people up and lead them into sin will certainly come. But how terrible for the one who brings them!
en.R: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "There will always be things that make people fall into sin. But how terrible it will be for the person who causes them!

es.L: Y dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Es imposible que no vengan los tropiezos, pero ¡ay de aquel por medio de quien vienen!
es.B: Jesús dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Es seguro que vendrán cosas que hacen tropezar a la gente y la llevan al pecado. Pero ¡ay de quien las provoque!
es.R: Jesús les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Siempre habrá cosas que hagan caer a la gente en el pecado. ¡Pero qué terrible será para la persona que las cause!

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il est impossible que les pierres d’achoppement n’arrivent pas, mais malheur [à celui] par qui elles arrivent !
fr.B: Jésus dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il arrivera forcément des choses qui font trébucher les gens et les entraînent dans le péché. Mais malheur à celui par qui elles arrivent !
fr.R: Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il y aura toujours des choses qui font tomber les gens dans le péché. Mais ce sera terrible pour celui qui en est la cause !

sw.L: Naye akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Haiwezekani vikwazo visije, lakini ole wake yule ambaye kupitia kwake vinakuja!
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Mambo yanayowakwaza watu na kuwaingiza dhambini hakika yatakuja. Lakini ole wake mtu anayeyaleta!
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Daima kutakuwa na mambo yanayowafanya watu waanguke dhambini. Lakini itakuwa vibaya sana kwa mtu anayeyasababisha!

vi.L: Ngài nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Không thể nào không có những cớ vấp ngã đến, nhưng khốn cho người mà cớ vấp ngã đến bởi người ấy!
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Những điều làm người ta vấp ngã và sa vào tội lỗi chắc chắn sẽ đến. Nhưng khốn cho kẻ gây ra những điều ấy!
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Sẽ luôn có những điều khiến người ta sa vào tội lỗi. Nhưng thật khốn khổ cho người nào gây ra những điều ấy!

ko.L: 그분이 그분의 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "걸림돌들이 오지 않을 수는 없다. 그러나 그것들을 오게 하는 사람에게는 화가 있다!
ko.B: 예수께서 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "사람을 걸려 넘어지게 해서 죄에 빠뜨리는 올무는 반드시 생긴다. 그러나 그것을 놓는 사람은 얼마나 불행하냐!
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "사람들을 죄짓게 하는 일은 언제나 있을 것이다. 그러나 그런 일을 일으키는 사람에게는 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다!

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos: "É impossível que não venham as ocasiões de tropeço, mas ai [daquele] por meio de quem elas vêm!
pt.B: Jesus disse aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos: "As armadilhas que fazem as pessoas tropeçar e cair no pecado certamente virão. Mas ai de quem as provocar!
pt.R: Jesus disse aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos: "Sempre vai haver coisas que levam as pessoas a pecar. Mas que terrível vai ser para quem causar essas coisas!

am.L: ለደቀ መዛሙርቱም እንዲህ አለ፦ «ማሰናከያዎች እንዳይመጡ አይቻልም፤ ነገር ግን ማሰናከያው በእርሱ በኩል ለሚመጣ [ሰው] ወዮለት!
am.B: ኢየሱስ ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ሰዎችን የሚያሰናክሉና ወደ ኃጢአት የሚመሩ ነገሮች መምጣታቸው አይቀርም። ነገር ግን እነርሱን ለሚያመጣ ሰው ወዮለት!
am.R: ኢየሱስ ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «ሰዎችን ኃጢአት እንዲሠሩ የሚያደርጉ ነገሮች ሁልጊዜ ይኖራሉ። ነገር ግን እነዚህን ነገሮች ለሚያመጣ ሰው ምንኛ አስከፊ ይሆንበታል!

decisions.choice: stumbling blocks: things that make someone fall into sin or give up faith
decisions.reason: The word first meant the trigger of a trap, then anything that makes a person trip. In the Gospels it means something that leads a person into sin or away from God (7:23). The next verse shows that the danger is to "these little ones".

decisions.choice: it is impossible for them not to come: they are certain to come
decisions.reason: The phrase says the thing cannot be avoided. In a world like this one, people will be led into sin; the warning is for whoever does the leading.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over someone headed for judgment
decisions.reason: As in 6:24-26 and 11:42-52, the word mourns and warns at once.

decisions.choice: woe (L); how terrible (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:24-26 and 11:42: Literal keeps "woe"; Balanced and Readable use an everyday expression of grief and warning.

decisions.choice: things that trip people up and lead them into sin (B); things that make people fall into sin (R)
decisions.reason: "Stumbling block" is church language. Balanced keeps the picture of tripping and says where it leads; Readable gives the sense.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:4
alternatives: a separate quotation for each verse
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 17:1-4 are one saying; the apostles speak in 17:5.

decisions.choice: ¡ay! (L, B); ¡qué terrible será...! (R)
alternatives: ¡qué terrible! at Balanced, as the English
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "¡ay!" is the cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m3), and it still reads naturally in a public reading, so Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced says "how terrible". Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal (17:37)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 2 and 4: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, including the days of Noah and of Lot that Jesus recalls in 17:26-29. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: malheur à celui (L, B); ce sera terrible pour celui (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps the traditional cry "malheur" at Literal and Balanced, where it is still current French for a warning of judgment (m3); Readable follows the English "how terrible". The generic "celui par qui" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: ole (L, B); itakuwa vibaya sana (R)
alternatives: itakuwa vibaya sana at Balanced, as the English
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "ole" is the cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m3), and it reads naturally in a public reading, so Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced says "how terrible". Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "cớ vấp ngã" (L); "những điều làm người ta vấp ngã" (B); "những điều khiến người ta sa vào tội lỗi" (R); "khốn cho" (L, B), "thật khốn khổ cho" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:7, the parallel saying: Literal keeps the stumbling block, and Readable says what it does. Balanced keeps the verb "vấp ngã" so the link with 17:2 is heard.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Luke 17; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시- ("그분" at Literal), Jesus speaks in 해라체, people speak to him in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (Korean style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "걸림돌" (L); "올무" (B); "죄짓게 하는 일" (R) for skandalon; "화가 있다" (L), "얼마나 불행하냐" (B), "끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다" (R) for ouai
decisions.reason: The wording of the parallel Korean Matthew 18:7; Literal keeps the picture of the stone, Balanced that of a snare. Readable follows Matthew 18:7 for ouai rather than Luke 6:24, since here the woe falls on one who causes others to sin.

decisions.choice: ocasiões de tropeço (L); armadilhas que fazem as pessoas tropeçar e cair no pecado (B)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:7. "Escândalo" is the old rendering, but to a Brazilian reader today it means a public scandal. Literal keeps the picture of tripping (m1); Balanced keeps the trap and says where it leads.

decisions.choice: ai (L, B); que terrível vai ser (R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "ai de" is still a living cry of grief and warning, unlike English "woe", so Balanced keeps it (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6), as in Matthew 18:7; Readable follows the English "how terrible".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: "ደቀ መዛሙርቱ" (his disciples) is written once
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span on each pronoun
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Amharic. This holds for the whole of Luke 17.

decisions.choice: ማሰናከያዎች (stumbling blocks, L); ወዮለት (woe to him, L, B); ምንኛ አስከፊ ይሆንበታል (how terrible it will be for him, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:7: "ወዮ" is the Amharic cry of grief and warning; Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling blocks do, as the English does.

source.text: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ λίθος μυλικὸς περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα.

records.literal_gloss: It is better for him if a stone of a mill is hung around the neck of him and he is thrown into the sea than that he should cause to stumble of these little ones one.

en.L: It is better for {{gender:that person|him}} if a millstone is hung around {{gender:their|his}} neck and {{gender:they are|he is}} thrown into the sea, than that {{gender:they|he}} should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
en.B: It would be better for {{gender:that person|him}} to be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around {{gender:their|his}} neck than to make one of these little ones stumble.
en.R: It would be better for {{gender:that person|him}} to have a heavy stone tied around {{gender:their|his}} neck and be thrown into the sea. That would be better than causing one of these little ones to sin.

es.L: Le es de más provecho si una piedra de molino [le] rodea el cuello y se le ha arrojado al mar, que hacer tropezar a uno de estos pequeños.
es.B: Más le valdría a esa persona ser arrojada al mar con una piedra de molino atada al cuello que hacer tropezar a uno de estos pequeños.
es.R: Sería mejor para esa persona que le ataran al cuello una piedra pesada y la tiraran al mar. Eso sería mejor que hacer pecar a uno de estos pequeños.

fr.L: Il vaut mieux pour lui qu’une meule de moulin soit placée autour de son cou et qu’il soit jeté dans la mer, plutôt qu’il fasse trébucher un seul de ces petits.
fr.B: Il vaudrait mieux pour lui être jeté dans la mer avec une meule attachée au cou que de faire trébucher un seul de ces petits.
fr.R: Il vaudrait mieux pour lui qu’on lui attache une grosse pierre autour du cou et qu’on le jette dans la mer. Ce serait mieux que de faire tomber dans le péché un de ces petits.

sw.L: Ni afadhali kwake ikiwa jiwe la kusagia limezungushwa shingoni mwake, naye ametupwa baharini, kuliko kwamba amkwaze mmoja wa wadogo hawa.
sw.B: Ingekuwa afadhali kwa mtu huyo kutupwa baharini akiwa amefungwa jiwe la kusagia shingoni, kuliko kumkwaza mmoja wa wadogo hawa.
sw.R: Ingekuwa afadhali kwa mtu huyo afungwe jiwe zito shingoni na kutupwa baharini. Hilo lingekuwa bora kuliko kumfanya mmoja wa wadogo hawa atende dhambi.

vi.L: Thà người ấy bị đeo cối đá vào cổ và bị ném xuống biển còn có lợi cho người ấy hơn là làm cho một trong những người nhỏ bé này vấp ngã.
vi.B: Thà người ấy bị buộc một cối đá vào cổ rồi bị ném xuống biển, còn hơn là làm cho một trong những người nhỏ bé này vấp ngã.
vi.R: Thà người ấy bị buộc một hòn đá nặng vào cổ rồi bị ném xuống biển. Như thế còn tốt cho người ấy hơn là làm cho một trong những người nhỏ bé này phạm tội.

ko.L: 그가 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나를 걸려 넘어지게 하는 것보다는, 연자 맷돌이 그의 목에 매달려 그가 바다에 던져지는 것이 그에게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 죄짓게 하느니, 차라리 큰 맷돌을 목에 매달고 바다에 던져지는 편이 그 사람에게 더 낫다.
ko.R: 그런 사람은 아주 무거운 맷돌을 목에 매단 채 바다에 던져지는 것이 더 낫다. 그것이 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나를 죄짓게 하는 것보다 낫다.

pt.L: Seria melhor para ele que uma pedra de moinho lhe fosse pendurada ao pescoço e ele fosse lançado ao mar, do que fazer tropeçar um destes pequeninos.
pt.B: Seria melhor para essa pessoa ser lançada ao mar com uma pedra de moinho amarrada ao pescoço do que levar a pecar um destes pequeninos.
pt.R: Seria melhor para essa pessoa ter uma pedra pesada amarrada no pescoço e ser jogada no mar. Isso seria melhor do que fazer um destes pequeninos pecar.

am.L: የወፍጮ ድንጋይ በአንገቱ ተንጠልጥሎ ወደ ባሕር ቢጣል፣ ከእነዚህ ከታናናሾቹ አንዱን ከሚያሰናክል ይሻለዋል።
am.B: ከእነዚህ ታናናሾች አንዱን ከሚያሰናክል ይልቅ የወፍጮ ድንጋይ በአንገቱ ታሥሮ ወደ ባሕር ቢጣል ይሻለዋል።
am.R: ትልቅ ድንጋይ በአንገቱ ታሥሮ ወደ ባሕር ቢወረወር ይሻለዋል። ይህ ከእነዚህ ታናናሾች አንዱን ኃጢአት እንዲሠራ ከማድረግ ይሻላል።

decisions.choice: a millstone: a heavy round stone for grinding grain
decisions.reason: The word means a stone of a mill. A person tied to it would sink and never come up. The picture is of a death without hope of rescue.

decisions.choice: these little ones: disciples who are weak or of little account
decisions.reason: Jesus is speaking to his disciples (17:1). The phrase points to followers who are humble and easily hurt, whom God cares for (compare 10:21; 12:32). It may include children, but is not limited to them.

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: lead into sin or away from faith
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for stumbling blocks in 17:1.

decisions.choice: a heavy stone
decisions.reason: Readable describes the stone instead of naming it, since few readers have seen a millstone.

decisions.choice: be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around their neck (B)
alternatives: if a millstone is hung around their neck and they are thrown into the sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the simpler English order with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: le, se le (L); esa persona (B, R), with no gender setting
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: The English offers "that person" or "him". Spanish "le", "se le" and "esa persona" already speak of any man or woman, so the setting has nothing to change, as in Matthew 18:6.

decisions.choice: lui, son cou, il with no gender span
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer back to the generic "celui par qui" of 17:1, and French "son" does not mark the owner's sex, so French needs no setting where the English has "that person / their". The same holds for "ses affaires" (17:31) and "sa vie" (17:33).

decisions.choice: kwake, mtu huyo, with no gender span
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: The English offers "that person" or "him". "Kwake", "naye", "mtu huyo" and the subject prefix a- do not mark sex, so the setting has nothing to change in Swahili. The same in verses 3-4 ("ndugu") and 31-33.

decisions.choice: "người ấy", "mình" with no gender span (also 17:31, 17:33)
decisions.reason: "người ấy" (that person) and the reflexive "mình" already include men and women, so the English gender spans have no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: "연자 맷돌" (L), "큰 맷돌" (B), "아주 무거운 맷돌" (R); "걸려 넘어지게 하다" (L), "죄짓게 하다" (B, R); "그", "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: As the Korean Matthew 18:6. Korean refers to the person without a gendered pronoun, so the English gender spans have nothing to match (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: The comparison "than that he should cause ... to stumble" placed first (L)
decisions.reason: Korean puts what is compared before "-보다는"; the sentence's parts are all kept.

decisions.choice: ele, o pescoço (L); essa pessoa (B, R), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English sets "that person/him" and "their/his". In Literal "ele" refers back to "aquele por meio de quem" in 17:1, the ordinary generic pronoun after such a phrase (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7), and Portuguese says "o pescoço" without a possessive; Balanced and Readable say "essa pessoa", which already includes anyone, as in Matthew 18:6.

decisions.choice: estes pequeninos
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:6: "pequeninos" plainly means people, the humble disciples of m2, where "estes pequenos" reads as an adjective waiting for its noun.

decisions.choice: ይሻለዋል, በአንገቱ (for him, his neck), with no gender span
alternatives: gender spans on the pronouns, as the English that person/him
decisions.reason: The pronouns are suffixes whose masculine form is also Amharic's general one for anyone, so there is no second wording for the setting to switch to; this holds for the general sayings of this chapter (17:4, 31, 33).

decisions.choice: ታናናሾች (little ones, the lowly)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:6: the word covers the lowly disciples the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of God's people, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in 6:41-42, the word is used of anyone in the same community of faith.

decisions.choice: rebuke: tell plainly that what was done is wrong
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak firmly against something. The aim is that the one who sinned will turn back, as the next words show.

decisions.choice: repent: turn away from the wrong and change one's mind about it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John and Jesus use for turning from sin to God (3:3; 5:32).

decisions.choice: if your brother sins: without "against you"
alternatives: if your brother sins against you
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "against you", perhaps from 17:4 or Matthew 18:15. Early witnesses such as Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus lack it, and the SBLGNT follows them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: warn (B); tell them it is wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Rebuke" can sound like an angry scolding. Balanced and Readable give the sense of speaking plainly to win the person back.

decisions.choice: turn away from the sin
decisions.reason: As in 3:3 and 5:32, Readable explains what repenting is.

decisions.choice: {{gender:tu hermano o hermana|tu hermano}}; "le" with no span
decisions.reason: The plural "hermanos" covers men and women, but the singular "tu hermano" names a man, and Jesus means any fellow disciple (meaning decision m1), so it takes the gender setting, as in Matthew 18:15. "Le" is the same for a man or a woman and needs no span. The same in verse 4.

decisions.choice: llámale la atención (L); adviértele (B); dile que lo que hizo está mal (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is telling someone plainly that what they did is wrong (meaning decision m2). "Reprender" takes "lo" or "la" and so would make the person a man or a woman; these verbs take "le", which covers both.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}}, then {{gender:il ou elle|il}} for the subject; "lui" with no span
decisions.reason: The brother is any fellow believer, man or woman (m1). The subject pronoun that agrees with the noun goes under the same setting, as the style guide asks; the object pronoun "lui" serves either sex, so Literal says "adresse-lui des reproches" rather than "reprends-le" and needs no span there. The same pattern carries into 17:4.

decisions.choice: se repentir (L, B); se détourner de son péché (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for the New Testament; Readable explains it as the English Readable does ("turn away from the sin").

decisions.choice: akitubu (L, B); akiiacha dhambi hiyo (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutubu" is the word for repent through Luke (meaning decision m3). Readable says what it means, turning away from the sin, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} for "brother"; "người ấy" for "him", with no span
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:15: a fellow member of God's people, man or woman (meaning decision), is "anh chị em" by default.

decisions.choice: "con" for the singular "you" (17:3-4)
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks to each disciple; as in Matthew 18:15, Jesus says "con".

decisions.choice: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} for adelphos, through 17:4; "그", "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: A fellow member of God's people, man or woman (meaning decision); the span settled in the Korean Matthew 18:15 and Luke 6:41. Korean needs no pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "꾸짖다" (L), "깨우쳐 주다" (B), "잘못이라고 말해 주다" (R); "회개하다" (L, B), "잘못에서 돌이키다" (R)
decisions.reason: To rebuke is to tell plainly that what was done is wrong (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: o seu {{gender:irmão ou irmã|irmão}}; {{gender:essa pessoa|ele}}, {{gender:ela|ele}}; perdoe-lhe, with no setting
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:15: the default is "irmão ou irmã" (m1), and the person is then "essa pessoa", "ela", with the traditional "o", "ele" as the alternative; the whole verb phrase goes under the setting where the clitic changes ("repreenda essa pessoa|repreenda-o"). "Perdoe-lhe" is the same for a man or a woman, so it needs no setting though the English has one; Readable says "perdoe" alone.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ወንድምህ ወይም እኅትህ|ወንድምህ}}; the pronouns with no span
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 18:15: the noun for a fellow believer takes the gender span, and the pronouns that follow are verb suffixes whose masculine form is also the general one.

records.literal_gloss: Said then the Lord, If you have faith like a grain of mustard, you would have said to the mulberry tree this, Be uprooted and be planted in the sea; and it would have obeyed you.

en.L: And the Lord said, "If you had faith like a grain of mustard, you would say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
en.B: The Lord answered, "If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could tell this mulberry tree, 'Tear yourself up by the roots and be planted in the sea,' and it would do as you say.
en.R: The Lord answered, "Even if your faith were only as big as a tiny mustard seed, you could say to this tree, 'Pull your roots out of the ground and go plant yourself in the sea!' And the tree would obey you.

es.L: Y dijo el Señor: «Si {{plural_you:tuvieran|tuvierais}} fe como un grano de mostaza, {{plural_you:dirían|diríais}} a este moral: “Sé arrancado de raíz y sé plantado en el mar”, y {{plural_you:les|os}} obedecería.
es.B: El Señor respondió: «Si {{plural_you:tuvieran|tuvierais}} una fe del tamaño de un grano de mostaza, {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} decirle a este moral: “Arráncate de raíz y plántate en el mar”, y {{plural_you:les|os}} haría caso.
es.R: El Señor les contestó: «Aunque {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe fuera tan pequeña como una diminuta semilla de mostaza, {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} decirle a este árbol: “¡Saca tus raíces de la tierra y ve a plantarte en el mar!”. Y el árbol {{plural_you:les|os}} obedecería.

fr.L: Et le Seigneur dit : « Si vous aviez de la foi comme un grain de moutarde, vous diriez à ce mûrier : “Sois déraciné et sois planté dans la mer”, et il vous obéirait.
fr.B: Le Seigneur répondit : « Si vous aviez de la foi gros comme une graine de moutarde, vous pourriez dire à ce mûrier : “Arrache-toi avec tes racines et va te planter dans la mer”, et il ferait ce que vous dites.
fr.R: Le Seigneur a répondu : « Même si votre foi était aussi petite qu’une minuscule graine de moutarde, vous pourriez dire à cet arbre : “Arrache tes racines du sol et va te planter dans la mer !” Et l’arbre vous obéirait.

sw.L: Naye Bwana akasema, "Kama mngekuwa na imani kama chembe ya haradali, mngesema na mforsadi huu, 'Ng'olewa kwa mizizi, upandwe ndani ya bahari,' nao ungewatii.
sw.B: Bwana alijibu, "Kama mngekuwa na imani yenye ukubwa wa mbegu ya haradali, mngeweza kuuambia mforsadi huu, 'Jing'oe na mizizi yako, ukajipande baharini,' nao ungefanya mnavyosema.
sw.R: Bwana alijibu, "Hata kama imani yenu ingekuwa ndogo kama mbegu ndogo sana ya haradali, mngeweza kuuambia mti huu, 'Ng'oa mizizi yako kutoka ardhini ukajipande baharini!' Na mti huo ungewatii.

vi.L: Chúa nói: "Nếu các con có đức tin như một hạt cải, thì các con có thể nói với cây dâu này: 'Hãy bật rễ lên và trồng mình xuống biển,' và nó sẽ vâng lời các con.
vi.B: Chúa đáp: "Nếu các con có đức tin chỉ bằng một hạt cải, các con có thể bảo cây dâu này: 'Hãy tự nhổ rễ lên và đi trồng mình dưới biển,' thì nó cũng sẽ làm theo lời các con.
vi.R: Chúa Giê-xu trả lời: "Nếu đức tin của các con chỉ nhỏ như một hạt cải thôi, các con cũng có thể nói với cây này: 'Hãy nhổ rễ lên khỏi đất và tự trồng mình xuống biển!' Và cây ấy sẽ vâng lời các con.

ko.L: 그러자 주님께서 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 겨자씨 한 알 같은 믿음이 있다면, 이 뽕나무에게 '뿌리째 뽑혀서 바다에 심어져라' 하고 말했을 것이다. 그러면 그것이 너희에게 순종했을 것이다.
ko.B: 주님께서 대답하셨다. "너희에게 겨자씨 한 알만 한 믿음이라도 있다면, 이 뽕나무더러 '뿌리째 뽑혀서 바다에 심겨라' 하고 말할 수 있을 것이다. 그러면 그 나무가 너희 말대로 할 것이다.
ko.R: 주 예수께서 대답하셨다. "너희 믿음이 아주 작은 겨자씨 한 알만큼밖에 안 된다고 해 보자. 그래도 너희가 이 나무에게 '뿌리를 뽑고 가서 바다에 심겨라!' 하고 말할 수 있을 것이다. 그러면 그 나무가 너희 말을 들을 것이다.

pt.L: E o Senhor disse: "Se vocês tivessem fé como um grão de mostarda, diriam a esta amoreira: 'Arranque-se pela raiz e plante-se no mar', e ela obedeceria a vocês.
pt.B: O Senhor respondeu: "Se vocês tivessem fé do tamanho de uma semente de mostarda, poderiam dizer a esta amoreira: 'Arranque-se pela raiz e plante-se no mar', e ela faria o que vocês mandassem.
pt.R: O Senhor respondeu: "Mesmo que a fé de vocês fosse só do tamanho de uma sementinha de mostarda, vocês poderiam dizer a esta árvore: 'Saia do chão com raiz e tudo e vá crescer no mar!' E a árvore obedeceria a vocês.

am.L: ጌታም እንዲህ አለ፦ «የሰናፍጭ ቅንጣት የምታክል እምነት ቢኖራችሁ ይህን የእንጆሪ ዛፍ፦ “ተነቀልና በባሕር ውስጥ ተተከል” ባላችሁት ነበር፤ እርሱም በታዘዘላችሁ ነበር።
am.B: ጌታም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰ፦ «የሰናፍጭ ቅንጣት የምታክል እምነት ቢኖራችሁ ኖሮ ይህን የእንጆሪ ዛፍ፦ “ከሥርህ ተነቅለህ በባሕር ውስጥ ተተከል” ልትሉት ትችሉ ነበር፤ እርሱም የምትሉትን ያደርግ ነበር።
am.R: ጌታም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «እምነታችሁ እንደ ትንሿ የሰናፍጭ ቅንጣት ብቻ ብትሆን እንኳ ይህን ዛፍ፦ “ሥርህን ከመሬት ነቅለህ ሂድና ራስህን በባሕር ውስጥ ትከል!” ልትሉት ትችሉ ነበር። ዛፉም ይታዘዛችሁ ነበር።

decisions.choice: faith: trust in God
decisions.reason: The point is not how much faith a person has, but that faith trusts God, for whom nothing is impossible (1:37).

decisions.choice: a grain of mustard: the mustard seed, known for being tiny
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was the smallest seed a farmer sowed (13:19). Even the smallest true faith is enough.

decisions.choice: mulberry tree: the black mulberry, a tree with deep, strong roots
decisions.reason: Luke uses a different word for the sycamore-fig that Zacchaeus climbs. This tree was known for roots that were hard to pull up.

decisions.choice: if you had faith: a condition that does not match the facts as they are
alternatives: if you have faith, as you do
decisions.reason: The verb in the "if" part is present, but the rest is put as something that would happen. Jesus implies that the apostles' faith is not even that small seed; the question is not how much faith, but whether it is real trust.

decisions.choice: be uprooted and planted in the sea: doing what seems impossible
alternatives: a promise of literal miracles with trees
decisions.reason: A tree planted in the sea is a deliberately impossible picture, to show what God can do through those who trust him.

decisions.choice: this tree
decisions.reason: Readable does not name the kind of tree; the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:10
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer to the apostles runs on without a break.

decisions.choice: moral (L, B); este árbol (R)
decisions.reason: The tree is the black mulberry, with deep, strong roots (meaning decision m3); in Spanish that tree is the "moral". "Sicómoro" is a different tree, a kind of fig. Readable says "this tree", as the English does.

decisions.choice: mforsadi (L, B); mti huu (R)
decisions.reason: The tree is the black mulberry, with deep, strong roots (meaning decision m3), "mforsadi" in Swahili. "Mkuyu" is the sycamore fig, a different tree. Readable says "this tree", as the English does. A reviewer should check that "mforsadi" is widely known.

decisions.choice: "cây dâu" (L, B); "cây này" (R) for the mulberry tree
decisions.reason: The black mulberry (meaning decision) is a kind of "cây dâu"; Readable leaves the kind out, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "겨자씨 한 알"; "뽕나무" (L, B), "이 나무" (R)
decisions.reason: "겨자씨 한 알" as the Korean Matthew 17:20; the black mulberry is a kind of "뽕나무" (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: amoreira (L, B); árvore (R)
decisions.reason: The tree is the black mulberry (m3), "amoreira" in Portuguese, known to Brazilian readers; it is kept distinct from the "sicômoro" Zacchaeus climbs (19:4). Readable says "árvore", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Arranque-se ... plante-se (L, B); Saia ... vá (R): the "você" imperative
decisions.reason: A command to a tree takes the form Jesus uses to one hearer, "você" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), as when he speaks to the fig tree (Matthew 21:19; Mark 11:14).

decisions.choice: የእንጆሪ ዛፍ (mulberry tree, L, B); ዛፍ (tree, R)
decisions.reason: "እንጆሪ" is the mulberry; "ሾላ" is a fig tree and would confuse it with the sycomore of 19:4. Readable says "tree" as the English does.

decisions.choice: ባላችሁት ነበር ... በታዘዘላችሁ ነበር (you would have said ... it would have obeyed)
decisions.reason: The Amharic unreal conditional keeps the Greek form that does not match the facts as they are (m4).

source.text: Τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλον ἔχων ἀροτριῶντα ἢ ποιμαίνοντα, ὃς εἰσελθόντι ἐκ τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Εὐθέως παρελθὼν ἀνάπεσε, ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Ἑτοίμασον τί δειπνήσω καὶ περιζωσάμενος διακόνει μοι ἕως φάγω καὶ πίω, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φάγεσαι καὶ πίεσαι σύ;

records.literal_gloss: Which now of you having a slave plowing or shepherding, who having come in out of the field will say to him, Immediately having come recline? \v 8 But not will he say to him, Prepare what I may eat, and having girded yourself serve me while I eat and drink, and after these things will eat and drink you?

en.L: Which of you, having a slave plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he has come in from the field, 'Come at once and recline [at table]'? \v 8 But will he not say to him, 'Prepare something for me to eat, and get dressed and serve me while I eat and drink, and after that you will eat and drink'?
en.B: Imagine that one of you has a servant who has been out plowing or tending the sheep. When he comes in from the field, will you tell him, 'Come straight in and take your place at the table'? \v 8 Will you not tell him instead, 'Make me something to eat. Then tie on your apron and serve me while I have my meal. You can eat and drink afterward'?
en.R: Let us say one of you has a servant who works out in the field, plowing or caring for sheep. When the servant comes in from work, you do not say to him, 'Come and sit down to eat right now.' \v 8 Instead, you say, 'Get my dinner ready. Put on your work clothes and serve me while I eat and drink. After that you can have your own meal.'

es.L: ¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, teniendo un esclavo que ara o pastorea, le dirá cuando él vuelve del campo: “Pasa en seguida y recuéstate [a la mesa]”? \v 8 ¿No le dirá más bien: “Prepárame algo para cenar, cíñete y sírveme mientras como y bebo, y después de esto comerás y beberás tú”?
es.B: {{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} que uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tiene un siervo que ha estado arando o cuidando las ovejas. Cuando el siervo vuelve del campo, ¿acaso le dirá: “Entra ya y siéntate a la mesa”? \v 8 ¿No le dirá más bien: “Prepárame la cena. Luego ponte el delantal y sírveme mientras como y bebo. Después podrás comer y beber tú”?
es.R: Supongamos que uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tiene un siervo que trabaja en el campo, arando o cuidando ovejas. Cuando el siervo vuelve del trabajo, no le dice: “Ven ahora mismo a sentarte a comer”. \v 8 Más bien le dice: “Prepárame la cena. Ponte la ropa de trabajo y sírveme mientras como y bebo. Después podrás comer tú”.

fr.L: Qui d’entre vous, ayant un esclave qui laboure ou qui garde les troupeaux, lui dira quand il rentre des champs : “Viens vite t’étendre [à table]” ? \v 8 Ne lui dira-t-il pas plutôt : “Prépare-moi de quoi dîner, ceins-toi et sers-moi pendant que je mange et que je bois ; et après cela, toi, tu mangeras et tu boiras” ?
fr.B: Imaginez que l’un de vous ait un serviteur qui laboure ou qui garde les moutons. Quand il revient des champs, lui direz-vous : “Viens vite prendre place à table” ? \v 8 Ne lui direz-vous pas plutôt : “Prépare-moi à manger. Puis mets ton tablier et sers-moi pendant que je prends mon repas. Tu mangeras et tu boiras ensuite” ?
fr.R: Supposons que l’un de vous ait un serviteur qui travaille dehors, dans les champs : il laboure ou il s’occupe des moutons. Quand le serviteur rentre du travail, vous ne lui dites pas : “Viens tout de suite t’asseoir pour manger.” \v 8 Au contraire, vous lui dites : “Prépare mon dîner. Mets tes vêtements de travail et sers-moi pendant que je mange et que je bois. Après, tu pourras prendre ton propre repas.”

sw.L: Lakini ni nani kati yenu, mwenye mtumwa anayelima au kuchunga, atakayemwambia akiingia kutoka shambani, 'Pita mara moja, uketi [chakulani]'? \v 8 Je, hatamwambia badala yake, 'Niandalie kitu cha kula, ujifunge mshipi unitumikie hadi nimalize kula na kunywa, na baada ya hayo wewe utakula na kunywa'?
sw.B: Fikirini mmoja wenu ana mtumishi aliyekuwa akilima au akichunga kondoo. Anaporudi kutoka shambani, je, atamwambia, 'Njoo moja kwa moja uketi mezani'? \v 8 Je, hatamwambia badala yake, 'Niandalie chakula. Kisha jifunge kibwebwe unihudumie ninapokula na kunywa. Wewe utakula na kunywa baadaye'?
sw.R: Tuseme mmoja wenu ana mtumishi anayefanya kazi shambani, akilima au akichunga kondoo. Mtumishi huyo akirudi kutoka kazini, hamwambii, 'Njoo uketi ule sasa hivi.' \v 8 Badala yake anamwambia, 'Niandalie chakula changu. Vaa nguo zako za kazi, unihudumie ninapokula na kunywa. Baada ya hapo utakula chakula chako.'

vi.L: Ai trong các con có một nô lệ đang cày ruộng hoặc chăn chiên, khi người ấy từ ngoài đồng về lại nói với người ấy: 'Hãy đến ngay và ngả mình [dùng bữa]'? \v 8 Chẳng phải sẽ nói với người ấy: 'Hãy dọn cho ta ăn, rồi thắt lưng lại mà hầu ta cho đến khi ta ăn uống xong, sau đó anh sẽ ăn uống' sao?
vi.B: Giả sử một người trong các con có một đầy tớ đi cày ruộng hoặc chăn chiên. Khi người đầy tớ ấy từ ngoài đồng về, các con có bảo: 'Vào ngay đi, ngồi vào bàn mà ăn' không? \v 8 Chẳng phải các con sẽ bảo: 'Hãy làm bữa cho ta ăn. Rồi buộc tạp dề vào mà phục vụ ta cho đến khi ta ăn uống xong. Sau đó anh hãy ăn uống' sao?
vi.R: Hãy nghĩ thế này: một người trong các con có một đầy tớ làm việc ngoài đồng, đi cày ruộng hoặc chăn chiên. Khi người đầy tớ ấy làm xong việc trở về, các con không bảo: 'Hãy ngồi xuống ăn ngay đi.' \v 8 Nhưng các con sẽ bảo: 'Hãy dọn bữa tối cho ta. Mặc quần áo làm việc vào và phục vụ ta trong khi ta ăn uống. Xong rồi anh hãy ăn phần của mình.'

ko.L: 너희 가운데 누가 밭을 갈거나 양을 치는 종이 있는데, 그가 들에서 들어올 때에 그에게 '어서 와서 [식탁에] 앉아라' 하고 말하겠느냐? \v 8 오히려 그에게 '내가 먹을 것을 준비하고, 허리를 동이고 내가 먹고 마시는 동안 내 시중을 들어라. 그 뒤에 너는 먹고 마셔라' 하고 말하지 않겠느냐?
ko.B: 너희 가운데 누가 밭을 갈거나 양을 치는 종을 두었다고 하자. 그 종이 들에서 일하고 들어왔을 때, 주인이 '어서 와서 식탁에 앉아라' 하고 말하겠느냐? \v 8 오히려 '내가 먹을 것을 차려라. 그리고 앞치마를 두르고 내가 먹고 마시는 동안 시중을 들어라. 너는 그다음에 먹고 마셔라' 하고 말하지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 너희 가운데 누가 종을 두고 있는데, 그 종이 들에서 밭을 갈거나 양을 치다가 들어왔다고 하자. 너희는 그 종에게 '어서 와서 앉아 밥을 먹어라' 하고 말하지 않는다. \v 8 오히려 '내 저녁을 차려라. 일할 옷을 입고 내가 먹고 마시는 동안 시중을 들어라. 너는 그다음에 먹어라' 하고 말한다.

pt.L: Quem de vocês, tendo um escravo que ara a terra ou pastoreia ovelhas, lhe dirá, quando ele voltar do campo: 'Venha logo e recline-se [à mesa]'? \v 8 Pelo contrário, não lhe dirá: 'Prepare-me algo para jantar, cinja-se e sirva-me enquanto eu como e bebo; e depois disso você comerá e beberá'?
pt.B: Imaginem que um de vocês tem um servo que esteve arando a terra ou cuidando das ovelhas. Quando ele chega do campo, será que você vai lhe dizer: 'Venha logo e sente-se à mesa'? \v 8 Em vez disso, você não vai dizer: 'Prepare o meu jantar. Depois ponha o avental e sirva-me enquanto eu como e bebo. Você pode comer e beber depois'?
pt.R: Imaginem que um de vocês tem um servo que trabalha no campo, arando a terra ou cuidando das ovelhas. Quando o servo chega do trabalho, você não diz a ele: 'Venha logo sentar e comer.' \v 8 Em vez disso, você diz: 'Prepare o meu jantar. Vista a roupa de trabalho e sirva-me enquanto eu como e bebo. Depois disso você pode fazer a sua refeição.'

am.L: ከእናንተ ደግሞ የሚያርስ ወይም የሚያግድ ባሪያ ያለው፣ ከእርሻ በገባ ጊዜ፦ “ፈጥነህ ቀርበህ [ለማዕድ] ተቀመጥ” የሚለው ማን ነው? \v 8 ይልቁንም፦ “የምበላውን አዘጋጅልኝ፤ እስክበላና እስክጠጣም ድረስ ታጥቀህ አገልግለኝ፤ ከዚያ በኋላ አንተ ትበላለህ፤ ትጠጣለህም” አይለውምን?
am.B: ከእናንተ አንዱ በማረስ ወይም በጎችን በመጠበቅ የሚሠራ ባሪያ አለው እንበል። ባሪያው ከእርሻ ሲገባ “ቶሎ ና፤ ለማዕድ ተቀመጥ” ይለዋልን? \v 8 ይልቁንም “የምበላውን አዘጋጅልኝ። ከዚያም ሽርጥህን ታጥቀህ እስክበላና እስክጠጣ ድረስ አስተናግደኝ። አንተ ከዚያ በኋላ ትበላለህ፤ ትጠጣለህም” አይለውምን?
am.R: ከእናንተ አንዱ በእርሻ የሚሠራ፣ የሚያርስ ወይም በጎችን የሚጠብቅ ባሪያ አለው እንበል። ባሪያው ከሥራ ሲገባ ጌታው “አሁኑኑ ና፤ ተቀምጠህ ብላ” አይለውም። \v 8 ይልቁንም “ራቴን አዘጋጅልኝ። የሥራ ልብስህን ልበስና እስክበላና እስክጠጣ ድረስ አስተናግደኝ። ከዚያ በኋላ አንተ የራስህን ምግብ ትበላለህ” ይለዋል።

decisions.choice: slave: a person owned by a master and at his command
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a slave (12:37). A small farmer might own one slave who did the field work and the housework too.

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answers "no" and "yes"
decisions.reason: The first question expects "No, no one would say that"; the second expects "Yes, of course he would". Jesus draws on what everyone knew about masters and slaves.

decisions.choice: recline: lie on a couch at a meal
decisions.reason: At a meal people lay on their side around a low table. To tell a slave to recline would be to treat him as a guest.

decisions.choice: having girded yourself: tying up one's long robe to be ready for work
alternatives: putting on a belt for decoration
decisions.reason: A long robe was tucked up into the belt for work or serving (12:35, 37).

decisions.choice: Imagine that one of you (B); Let us say one of you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set up the picture first, then ask (B) or state (R) what the master does.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: Readable gives the expected answers as plain statements.

decisions.choice: take your place at the table; tie on your apron (B); sit down to eat; put on your work clothes (R)
decisions.reason: Modern readers sit at meals and do not tuck up robes; the meaning decisions explain the customs.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave". Balanced says "has a servant" rather than "owns".

decisions.choice: esclavo (L); siervo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man belongs to his master (meaning decision m1). Literal says "esclavo"; Balanced and Readable say "siervo", as the English says "servant", since the point is his duty, not slavery itself. The same through verse 10.

decisions.choice: un esclave (L); un serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and the English: Literal keeps that the man was owned (m1), Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", the word for one who works at a master's command. The same in 17:9-10.

decisions.choice: t’étendre [à table]; ceins-toi (L)
alternatives: mets-toi à table; attache ta ceinture
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the customs the meaning decisions explain: guests lay on couches at a meal (m3), and a servant tucked up his robe with a belt before working (m4). "Ceindre" is old but is the French word for that act; Balanced and Readable use today's pictures ("prendre place à table", "mets ton tablier").

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L); mtumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man belongs to his master (meaning decision m1). Literal says "mtumwa"; Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", as the English says "servant", since the point is his duty, not slavery itself. The same through verse 10.

decisions.choice: jifunge kibwebwe
decisions.reason: Tying up the robe to work (meaning decision m4) has a Swahili match: "kujifunga kibwebwe" is tying a cloth round the waist for hard work. Literal keeps the Greek picture with "ujifunge mshipi".

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos (17:7-10)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for doulos: the meaning decision keeps his position as one owned by a master, which Literal shows.

decisions.choice: "ta" for the master and "anh" for the servant in the master's words
decisions.reason: The master gives orders to one under him; "ta" keeps his authority, and "anh" avoids the archaic "ngươi", as in 16:2.

decisions.choice: "ngả mình [dùng bữa]" (L) for "recline"
decisions.reason: As in Luke 12:37: guests lay on couches at a meal (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say "ngồi", the Vietnamese way to take a place at a meal.

decisions.choice: "종" for doulos at every level, through 17:10
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 15:22; Korean "종" names one who belongs to a master, as the meaning decision says, without the modern picture that "노예" brings.

decisions.choice: "[식탁에] 앉아라" (L), "식탁에 앉아라" (B), "앉아 밥을 먹어라" (R); "허리를 동이고" (L), "앞치마를 두르고" (B), "일할 옷을 입고" (R)
decisions.reason: Reclining is taking one's place at a meal, and girding is tying up one's robe for work (meaning decisions); Literal keeps the Greek's picture, and Korean names the table, which Literal brackets.

decisions.choice: Imaginem que um de vocês ... você
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the group ("vocês") and then pictures one of them as the master, whom Portuguese addresses as "você", the way a speaker turns to one listener; "vocês diriam" would make the whole group one master.

decisions.choice: ባሪያ (slave) at every level
alternatives: አገልጋይ (servant), as the English Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "ባሪያ" for doulos at every level; the point of the saying is that a slave is owed nothing for doing what he is told (17:9-10).

decisions.choice: the master's questions in the third person (ይለዋልን? the master says)
alternatives: "you" in the questions, as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: After "ከእናንተ አንዱ" (one of you) Amharic goes on about that person; the second person would read as a different speaker.

source.text: μὴ ἔχει χάριν τῷ δούλῳ ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὰ διαταχθέντα;

records.literal_gloss: Not does he have thanks to the slave because he did the things having been commanded?

en.L: He does not have thanks for the slave because he did the things commanded, does he?
en.B: The master does not owe the servant any thanks for doing what he was ordered to do, does he?
en.R: The master does not thank the servant for doing what he was told to do.

es.L: ¿Acaso da gracias al esclavo porque hizo lo que se le ordenó?
es.B: El amo no le debe ningún agradecimiento al siervo por hacer lo que se le ordenó, ¿verdad?
es.R: El amo no le da las gracias al siervo por hacer lo que le mandaron.

fr.L: A-t-il de la reconnaissance pour l’esclave parce qu’il a fait ce qui avait été ordonné ?
fr.B: Le maître ne doit pas de remerciements au serviteur parce qu’il a fait ce qu’on lui avait commandé, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Le maître ne remercie pas le serviteur d’avoir fait ce qu’on lui avait demandé.

sw.L: Je, ana shukrani kwa mtumwa kwa sababu alifanya yale aliyoamriwa?
sw.B: Yule bwana hana deni la shukrani kwa mtumishi wake kwa kufanya aliyoagizwa, sivyo?
sw.R: Yule bwana hamshukuru mtumishi kwa kufanya kile alichoambiwa.

vi.L: [Người chủ] đâu có mang ơn người nô lệ vì người ấy đã làm những điều được truyền bảo, phải không?
vi.B: Người chủ đâu có mang ơn người đầy tớ vì anh ta đã làm những việc được giao, phải không?
vi.R: Người chủ không cảm ơn người đầy tớ vì đã làm những việc mình được bảo phải làm.

ko.L: 종이 명령받은 일을 했다고 해서 주인이 그 종에게 고마워하겠느냐?
ko.B: 종이 시킨 일을 했다고 해서 주인이 그 종에게 고마워할 까닭이 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 주인은 종이 시킨 일을 했다고 해서 고맙다고 하지 않는다.

pt.L: Por acaso ele fica agradecido ao escravo porque fez as coisas ordenadas?
pt.B: O dono não deve nenhum agradecimento ao servo por ter feito o que lhe mandaram, deve?
pt.R: O dono não agradece ao servo por ele ter feito o que lhe mandaram.

am.L: ባሪያውን የታዘዘውን ስላደረገ ያመሰግነዋልን?
am.B: ባሪያው የታዘዘውን በማድረጉ ጌታው የምስጋና ዕዳ አለበትን?
am.R: ጌታው ባሪያውን የታዘዘውን ስላደረገ አያመሰግነውም።

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude owed to someone
decisions.reason: The noun usually translated "grace" also means thanks. With the verb "have" it is the usual way to say "be grateful" (1 Timothy 1:12). Here it is thanks, not God's grace.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: As in 17:7.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The form of the question expects "No, he does not".

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable gives the expected answer as a plain statement.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "주인이" (L) without brackets
decisions.reason: The Greek subject "he" is the master; Korean must name him, and "주인" stands for the Greek pronoun rather than an added word.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ποιήσητε πάντα τὰ διαταχθέντα ὑμῖν, λέγετε ὅτι Δοῦλοι ἀχρεῖοί ἐσμεν, ὃ ὠφείλομεν ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Thus also you, when you may have done all the things having been commanded you, say, Slaves unworthy are we; that which we were bound to do we have done.

en.L: So also you, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, 'We are unworthy slaves; what we were obligated to do, we have done.'"
en.B: It is the same with you. When you have done everything you were ordered to do, say, 'We are unworthy servants. We have done no more than we were bound to do.'"
en.R: It is the same with you. When you have done all that you were told to do, you should say, 'We are only servants, and we have earned nothing special. We have just done the work we were supposed to do.'"

es.L: Así también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, cuando {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} hecho todo lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} ordenó, {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “Somos esclavos sin mérito; lo que estábamos obligados a hacer, [eso] hemos hecho”».
es.B: Lo mismo pasa con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Cuando {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} hecho todo lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} ordenó, {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: “Somos siervos que no merecen nada especial. No hemos hecho más que lo que debíamos”».
es.R: Lo mismo pasa con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Cuando {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} hecho todo lo que se {{plural_you:les|os}} mandó, {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} decir: “Solo somos siervos, y no nos hemos ganado nada especial. Solo hemos hecho el trabajo que nos tocaba hacer”».

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi, quand vous aurez fait tout ce qui vous a été ordonné, dites : “Nous sommes des esclaves sans mérite ; ce que nous devions faire, nous l’avons fait.” »
fr.B: Il en va de même pour vous. Quand vous aurez fait tout ce qui vous a été ordonné, dites : “Nous sommes des serviteurs sans mérite. Nous n’avons fait que ce que nous devions faire.” »
fr.R: C’est la même chose pour vous. Quand vous avez fait tout ce qu’on vous a demandé, vous devez dire : “Nous sommes seulement des serviteurs, et nous n’avons rien gagné de spécial. Nous avons juste fait le travail que nous devions faire.” »

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo nanyi, mtakapokuwa mmefanya yote mliyoamriwa, semeni, 'Sisi ni watumwa tusiostahili kitu; tumefanya kile tulichopaswa kufanya.'"
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo kwenu pia. Mkiisha kufanya yote mliyoagizwa, semeni, 'Sisi ni watumishi tusiostahili kitu cha ziada. Tumefanya tu yale tuliyopaswa kufanya.'"
sw.R: Ndivyo ilivyo kwenu pia. Mkimaliza kufanya yote mliyoambiwa, mnapaswa kusema, 'Sisi ni watumishi tu, na hatujajipatia kitu cha pekee. Tumefanya tu kazi tuliyotakiwa kufanya.'"

vi.L: Các con cũng vậy, khi đã làm xong mọi điều được truyền bảo cho các con, hãy nói: 'Chúng con là những nô lệ không có công gì; chúng con chỉ làm điều chúng con phải làm.'"
vi.B: Các con cũng vậy. Khi đã làm xong mọi việc được giao, hãy nói: 'Chúng con chỉ là những đầy tớ chẳng có công gì. Chúng con chỉ làm điều bổn phận phải làm mà thôi.'"
vi.R: Các con cũng vậy. Khi đã làm xong mọi việc mình được bảo phải làm, các con nên nói: 'Chúng con chỉ là đầy tớ, chẳng có công gì đặc biệt. Chúng con chỉ làm công việc mà mình phải làm.'"

ko.L: 이와 같이 너희도 너희에게 명령받은 일을 다 하고 나서, '저희는 쓸모없는 종입니다. 저희는 해야 할 일을 했을 뿐입니다' 하고 말하여라."
ko.B: 너희도 마찬가지다. 너희가 명령받은 일을 다 하고 나서, '저희는 보잘것없는 종입니다. 저희는 해야 할 일을 했을 뿐입니다' 하고 말하여라."
ko.R: 너희도 마찬가지다. 너희가 하라는 일을 다 했을 때에 이렇게 말해야 한다. '저희는 그저 종일 뿐입니다. 특별히 받을 것이 없습니다. 저희는 마땅히 해야 할 일을 했을 뿐입니다.'"

pt.L: Assim também vocês, quando tiverem feito tudo o que lhes foi ordenado, digam: 'Somos escravos indignos; fizemos o que devíamos fazer.'"
pt.B: O mesmo vale para vocês. Quando tiverem feito tudo o que lhes mandaram, digam: 'Somos servos que não merecem nada. Fizemos apenas o que era a nossa obrigação.'"
pt.R: O mesmo acontece com vocês. Quando tiverem feito tudo o que mandaram vocês fazerem, digam: 'Somos apenas servos e não merecemos nada especial. Só fizemos o trabalho que tínhamos de fazer.'"

am.L: እንዲሁ እናንተም የታዘዛችሁትን ሁሉ ባደረጋችሁ ጊዜ፦ “ዋጋ የሌለን ባሪያዎች ነን፤ ልናደርገው የሚገባንን አደረግን” በሉ።»
am.B: እናንተም እንዲሁ ናችሁ። የታዘዛችሁትን ሁሉ ባደረጋችሁ ጊዜ “ምንም የማይገባን ባሪያዎች ነን፤ ልናደርገው የሚገባንን ብቻ አደረግን” በሉ።»
am.R: እናንተም እንደዚሁ ናችሁ። የታዘዛችሁትን ሁሉ ባደረጋችሁ ጊዜ “እኛ ባሪያዎች ብቻ ነን፤ ለየት ያለ ዋጋ አይገባንም። ልንሠራው የሚገባንን ሥራ ብቻ ሠራን” ልትሉ ይገባል።»

decisions.choice: unworthy: having no special claim, owed nothing extra
decisions.reason: The word can mean useless (Matthew 25:30), but these slaves have done all they were told. Here it means they have earned no reward of their own; they have only done their duty. Any reward is the master's gift (compare 12:37).

decisions.choice: slaves: those who belong to their master
decisions.reason: The disciples stand before God as slaves before their master: all they do is already owed to him.

decisions.choice: what we were obligated to do: obedience is owed, not a favor done to God
alternatives: a statement that obedience does not matter
decisions.reason: The parable does not make obedience small. It answers the request for more faith (17:5): faith simply does what the Master asks, without claiming credit.

decisions.choice: only servants, and we have earned nothing special
decisions.reason: "Unworthy" can sound like "worthless". Readable gives the sense the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer, begun at 17:6, ends here.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: sin mérito (L); que no merecen nada especial (B); no nos hemos ganado nada especial (R)
decisions.reason: The word means having no special claim on the master (meaning decision m1). The familiar "inútiles" says they are useless, which is not the point.

decisions.choice: sans mérite (L, B)
decisions.reason: The word means having no special claim, owed nothing extra (m1). "Inutiles", the traditional French, says that the servants are of no use, which the parable does not say; "indignes" sounds like shame. "Sans mérite" says that they have earned nothing beyond their duty.

decisions.choice: tusiostahili kitu (L); tusiostahili kitu cha ziada (B); hatujajipatia kitu cha pekee (R)
decisions.reason: The word means having no special claim on the master (meaning decision m1). "Wasio na faida" would say they are useless, which is not the point.

decisions.choice: "không có công gì" (L); "chẳng có công gì" (B, R) for "unworthy"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as having no special claim, owed nothing extra; "vô dụng" (useless) would say the servants did poor work.

decisions.choice: "chúng con" in the words the disciples are to say
decisions.reason: The servants of the saying stand for the disciples before God (meaning decision); "chúng con" is how disciples speak to their Lord in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "쓸모없는 종" (L); "보잘것없는 종" (B); "그저 종일 뿐 ... 특별히 받을 것이 없다" (R); "저희" in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Unworthy here means having no special claim (meaning decision); Literal keeps the hard word. The disciples speak to their Master in the humble polite style.

decisions.choice: indignos (L); que não merecem nada (B)
decisions.reason: "Inúteis" is the familiar word, but these slaves have done all they were told (m1): they are not useless, only owed nothing extra. Literal says "indignos", Balanced says what it means.

decisions.choice: ዋጋ የሌለን (unworthy, L); ምንም የማይገባን (to whom nothing is owed, B); ለየት ያለ ዋጋ አይገባንም (we are owed no special reward, R)
decisions.reason: The sense is having no special claim (m1), not being useless; "ዋጋ" is the word for reward, as in Matthew.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ μέσον Σαμαρείας καὶ Γαλιλαίας.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the going to Jerusalem that he was passing through [the] midst of Samaria and Galilee.

en.L: And it happened, while going to Jerusalem, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
en.B: As Jesus made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way toward Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went through the region between Samaria and Galilee.
en.R: Jesus was still traveling toward Jerusalem. He went through the area where Samaria and Galilee meet.

es.L: Y sucedió que, yendo a Jerusalén, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pasaba por en medio de Samaria y Galilea.
es.B: Mientras Jesús seguía {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} camino hacia Jerusalén, pasó por la región que está entre Samaria y Galilea.
es.R: Jesús seguía viajando hacia Jerusalén. Pasó por la zona donde se juntan Samaria y Galilea.

fr.L: Et il arriva, en allant à Jérusalem, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passait par le milieu de la Samarie et de la Galilée.
fr.B: Tandis que Jésus faisait route vers Jérusalem, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passa par la région située entre la Samarie et la Galilée.
fr.R: Jésus était toujours en route vers Jérusalem. Il est passé par la région où la Samarie et la Galilée se touchent.

sw.L: Ikawa, alipokuwa akienda Yerusalemu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akipita katikati ya Samaria na Galilaya.
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akiendelea na safari {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuelekea Yerusalemu, alipita katika eneo lililo kati ya Samaria na Galilaya.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa bado akisafiri kwenda Yerusalemu. Alipita katika eneo ambapo Samaria na Galilaya zinapakana.

vi.L: Và xảy ra, trên đường đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi qua giữa Sa-ma-ri và Ga-li-lê.
vi.B: Trên đường đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, Đức Giê-xu đi qua vùng giáp ranh giữa Sa-ma-ri và Ga-li-lê.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu vẫn đang trên đường đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ngài đi qua vùng giáp ranh giữa Sa-ma-ri và Ga-li-lê.

ko.L: 그리고 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그분이 예루살렘으로 가시는 길에 사마리아와 갈릴리 사이를 지나가고 계셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 예루살렘으로 가시는 길에 사마리아와 갈릴리 사이의 지역을 지나가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 여전히 예루살렘을 향해 가고 계셨다. 예수께서 사마리아와 갈릴리가 맞닿은 지역을 지나가셨다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, indo para Jerusalém, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} passava pelo meio de Samaria e da Galileia.
pt.B: Seguindo o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} caminho para Jerusalém, Jesus passou pela região que fica entre Samaria e a Galileia.
pt.R: Jesus continuava viajando para Jerusalém. Ele passou pela região na divisa entre Samaria e a Galileia.

am.L: ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምም ሲሄድ እንዲህ ሆነ፤ እርሱ በሰማርያና በገሊላ መካከል ያልፍ ነበር።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ሲጓዝ በሰማርያና በገሊላ መካከል ባለው አገር አለፈ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ አሁንም ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም እየተጓዘ ነበር። ሰማርያና ገሊላ በሚገናኙበት አካባቢ አለፈ።

decisions.choice: through the middle of Samaria and Galilee: along the region between the two
alternatives: through Samaria and then through Galilee
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. Galilee lay north of Samaria, and a traveler going toward Jerusalem would not pass through Samaria and then Galilee. The likely sense is that Jesus went along the border land between them, which suits a story with both a Samaritan and Jews in it.

decisions.choice: going to Jerusalem: the journey Jesus set out on at 9:51
decisions.reason: Luke reminds the reader that Jesus is on his way to Jerusalem, where he will suffer (9:51; 13:22).

decisions.choice: the region between (B); the area where Samaria and Galilee meet (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likely sense, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "사마리아와 갈릴리 사이" (L, B); "사마리아와 갈릴리가 맞닿은 지역" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision (footnoted) reads the phrase as the region between the two; Korean "사이" says that at every level.

source.text: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ἀπήντησαν δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες, οἳ ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦραν φωνὴν λέγοντες· Ἰησοῦ ἐπιστάτα, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: And on the entering of him into a certain village met [him] ten leprous men, who stood afar off, \v 13 and they lifted up [their] voice saying, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered a certain village, ten leprous men met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who stood far off; \v 13 and they lifted up [their] voice, saying, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came into a village, ten men with leprosy came toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They kept their distance \v 13 and called out loudly, "Jesus! Master! Have mercy on us!"
en.R: As Jesus was going into a village, ten men with a terrible skin disease came toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They stood far away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 13 They shouted, "Jesus! Master! Please have mercy on us!"

es.L: Y al entrar {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en cierta aldea, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} salieron al encuentro diez hombres leprosos, que se pararon de lejos, \v 13 y ellos alzaron [la] voz, diciendo: «¡Jesús, Maestro, ten piedad de nosotros!».
es.B: Al entrar en una aldea, diez hombres con lepra salieron a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. Se quedaron a distancia \v 13 y gritaron con fuerza: «¡Jesús! ¡Maestro! ¡Ten piedad de nosotros!».
es.R: Cuando Jesús iba a entrar en una aldea, diez hombres con una grave enfermedad de la piel se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Se quedaron lejos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 13 Gritaron: «¡Jesús! ¡Maestro! ¡Por favor, ten compasión de nosotros!».

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entrait dans un village, dix hommes lépreux vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre ; ils s’arrêtèrent au loin \v 13 et ils élevèrent la voix en disant : « Jésus, Maître, aie pitié de nous ! »
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entrait dans un village, dix hommes atteints de la lèpre vinrent vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils restèrent à distance \v 13 et crièrent très fort : « Jésus ! Maître ! Aie pitié de nous ! »
fr.R: Au moment où Jésus entrait dans un village, dix hommes qui avaient une terrible maladie de peau sont venus vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils sont restés loin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \v 13 Ils ont crié : « Jésus ! Maître ! Aie pitié de nous, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît ! »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akiingia katika kijiji fulani, wanaume kumi wakoma walikutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, ambao walisimama mbali; \v 13 nao wakapaza sauti, wakisema, "Yesu, Mkuu, tuhurumie!"
sw.B: Alipokuwa akiingia katika kijiji kimoja, wanaume kumi wenye ukoma walimjia. Walisimama mbali, \v 13 wakapaza sauti, "Yesu! Mkuu! Tuhurumie!"
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akiingia katika kijiji, wanaume kumi wenye ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi walikuja kumwelekea. Walisimama mbali {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. \v 13 Walipiga kelele, "Yesu! Mkuu! Tafadhali tuhurumie!"

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào một làng kia, có mười người phung đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; họ đứng đằng xa \v 13 và cất tiếng nói: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, lạy Thầy, xin thương xót chúng tôi!"
vi.B: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào một làng kia, có mười người mắc bệnh ngoài da nặng đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ đứng đằng xa \v 13 và kêu lớn: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu! Lạy Thầy! Xin thương xót chúng tôi!"
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu đang đi vào một làng kia, có mười người bị bệnh phong, một bệnh ngoài da rất nặng, đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ đứng cách xa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 13 Họ kêu lớn: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, Thầy ơi! Xin thương xót chúng tôi!"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 어떤 마을에 들어가실 때에, 나병에 걸린 남자 열 명이 그분을 맞으러 왔다. 그들은 멀리 서서 \v 13 소리를 높여 말했다. "예수 선생님, 저희를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"
ko.B: 예수께서 어떤 마을에 들어가실 때에, 악성 피부병에 걸린 남자 열 명이 예수께로 왔다. 그들은 멀찍이 서서 \v 13 큰 소리로 외쳤다. "예수 선생님! 저희를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"
ko.R: 예수께서 어떤 마을에 들어가실 때에, 심한 피부병에 걸린 남자 열 명이 예수께로 왔다. 그들은 예수께 가까이 오지 않고 멀리 서 있었다. \v 13 그리고 크게 소리쳤다. "예수 선생님! 제발 저희를 불쌍히 여겨 주십시오!"

pt.L: E, ao entrar {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} num certo povoado, dez homens leprosos {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} encontraram, os quais ficaram parados de longe; \v 13 e eles levantaram a voz, dizendo: "Jesus, Mestre, tem misericórdia de nós!"
pt.B: Quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava entrando num povoado, dez homens com lepra vieram ao {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} encontro. Eles ficaram a distância \v 13 e gritaram bem alto: "Jesus! Mestre! Tem misericórdia de nós!"
pt.R: Jesus estava entrando num povoado quando dez homens com uma doença de pele terrível vieram na direção {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Eles ficaram longe {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. \v 13 Eles gritaram: "Jesus! Mestre! Por favor, tem pena de nós!"

am.L: ወደ አንዲት መንደርም ሲገባ ለምጻሞች የሆኑ አሥር ሰዎች ተገናኙት፤ እነርሱም በሩቅ ቆሙ፤ \v 13 ድምፃቸውንም ከፍ አድርገው፦ «ኢየሱስ፣ አለቃ ሆይ፣ ማረን!» አሉ።
am.B: ወደ አንዲት መንደር ሲገባ ለምጽ የያዛቸው አሥር ሰዎች ወደ እርሱ መጡ። እነርሱም ራቅ ብለው ቆሙ፤ \v 13 በታላቅ ድምፅም «ኢየሱስ ሆይ! አለቃችን! ማረን!» ብለው ጮኹ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ወደ አንዲት መንደር ሲገባ ከባድ የቆዳ በሽታ የነበረባቸው አሥር ሰዎች ወደ እርሱ መጡ። ከእርሱ ርቀው ቆሙ። \v 13 እነርሱም «ኢየሱስ ሆይ! አለቃችን! እባክህ ማረን!» እያሉ ጮኹ።

decisions.choice: leprous: having a serious skin disease that made a person unclean under the law
alternatives: having the disease now called leprosy only
decisions.reason: As at 5:12. The law of Moses required such people to live apart and to warn others away (Leviticus 13:45-46).

decisions.choice: stood far off: kept the distance the law required
decisions.reason: Because of their disease they could not come near other people (Leviticus 13:46).

decisions.choice: Master: one with authority, who gives orders
decisions.reason: This is the disciples' word for Jesus in Luke (5:5; 8:24). Only here does someone outside the disciples use it.

decisions.choice: have mercy on us: take pity on us and help us
decisions.reason: The cry asks for help in need, as the blind man asks in 18:38.

decisions.choice: a terrible skin disease
decisions.reason: As at 5:12: "leprosy" now means one particular disease.

decisions.choice: called out loudly
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the Hebrew-sounding idiom.

decisions.choice: hombres leprosos (L); hombres con lepra (B); hombres con una grave enfermedad de la piel (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 8:2: the Greek word covers several skin diseases that made a person unclean under the law (meaning decision m1). Readable describes it rather than naming modern leprosy, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Maestro
decisions.reason: Luke's word is for one in charge who gives orders (meaning decision m3), not the word for a teacher. "Jefe" sounds like a workplace and "Señor" is kept for the Lord, so "Maestro", the usual respectful address to a leader, is used; it is also the word for "Teacher" elsewhere. A reviewer should weigh it.

decisions.choice: Maître at every level
decisions.reason: Luke's word is for one with authority who gives orders (m3). French "Maître" carries that sense and is the usual address to Jesus; "Chef" or "Patron" would sound like a workplace. French also says "Maître" for "Teacher" (18:18), so the two Greek words are not told apart in French.

decisions.choice: lépreux (L); atteints de la lèpre (B); une terrible maladie de peau (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: today "la lèpre" names one disease, while the word covered several serious skin diseases (m1), so Readable describes it.

decisions.choice: wakoma (L); wenye ukoma (B); wenye ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 8:2: the Greek word covers several skin diseases that made a person unclean under the law (meaning decision m1). Readable describes it rather than naming modern leprosy, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Mkuu
decisions.reason: Luke's word is for one in charge who gives orders (meaning decision m3), not the word for a teacher ("Mwalimu"), and "Bwana" is kept for the Lord. "Mkuu" (chief, the one in charge) is respectful in address. A reviewer should weigh it.

decisions.choice: "người phung" (L); "người mắc bệnh ngoài da nặng" (B); "người bị bệnh phong, một bệnh ngoài da rất nặng" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 4:27, 5:12 and 7:22.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Đức Giê-xu, lạy Thầy" for "Jesus, Master"; "chúng tôi" for the men
decisions.reason: "Thầy" is the word settled for Luke's "Master" (5:5, 9:33); "Lạy" makes it a humble plea, as in Mark 10:47. The men are not disciples, so they say "chúng tôi".

decisions.choice: "나병" (L), "악성 피부병" (B), "심한 피부병" (R); "선생님" for epistata
decisions.reason: The disease words of the Korean Luke 5:12 and Mark 1:40; "선생님" for epistata as settled at Luke 5:5 and 8:24.

decisions.choice: Mestre
decisions.reason: The disciples' word for Jesus in Luke, as in 8:24. Portuguese "Mestre" also renders "Teacher" (18:18), a distinction English can make and Portuguese cannot without an odd word; the meaning decision (m3) keeps it.

decisions.choice: tem misericórdia (L, B); tem pena (R)
decisions.reason: The men call to Jesus, so they use the "tu" imperative "tem", as the blind men do in Matthew 20:30 (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4).

decisions.choice: አለቃ ሆይ (L); አለቃችን (our master, B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke's word is the one who has authority and gives orders, not the word for teacher (didaskalos, "መምህር") nor kyrios ("ጌታ"); "አለቃ" keeps it distinct. A reviewer may prefer another word.

decisions.choice: ለምጻሞች (lepers, L); ለምጽ የያዛቸው (who had leprosy, B); ከባድ የቆዳ በሽታ የነበረባቸው (who had a serious skin disease, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 8:2: Balanced names the people rather than labelling them, and Readable says what the disease was, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen [them] he said to them, Having gone show yourselves to the priests.

en.L: And having seen [them], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Go, show yourselves to the priests."
en.B: Jesus saw them and told them, "Go and let the priests examine you."
en.R: When Jesus saw them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Go and let the priests look at your skin."

es.L: Y cuando [los] vio, les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:muéstrense|mostraos}} a los sacerdotes».
es.B: Jesús los vio y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que los sacerdotes {{plural_you:los|os}} examinen».
es.R: Cuando Jesús los vio, les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} y {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que los sacerdotes {{plural_you:les|os}} revisen la piel».

fr.L: Et, [les] ayant vus, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Allez vous montrer aux prêtres. »
fr.B: Jésus les vit et leur dit : « Allez vous faire examiner par les prêtres. »
fr.R: Quand Jésus les a vus, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a dit : « Allez montrer votre peau aux prêtres. »

sw.L: Naye alipowaona, akawaambia, "Nendeni, mjioneshe kwa makuhani."
sw.B: Yesu aliwaona, akawaambia, "Nendeni mkachunguzwe na makuhani."
sw.R: Yesu alipowaona, aliwaambia, "Nendeni makuhani waangalie ngozi yenu."

vi.L: Và thấy [họ], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Hãy đi, trình diện mình với các thầy tế lễ."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu thấy họ thì bảo: "Hãy đi để các thầy tế lễ khám cho các anh."
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu thấy họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Hãy đi và để các thầy tế lễ xem da của các anh."

ko.L: 그분이 [그들을] 보시고 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "가서 제사장들에게 너희 몸을 보여라."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들을 보시고 말씀하셨다. "가서 제사장들에게 몸을 보이고 검사를 받아라."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들을 보시고 말씀하셨다. "가서 제사장들에게 너희 피부를 보여라."

pt.L: E, quando [os] viu, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Vão e mostrem-se aos sacerdotes."
pt.B: Jesus os viu e lhes disse: "Vão e deixem os sacerdotes examinar vocês."
pt.R: Quando Jesus os viu, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Vão e deixem os sacerdotes olhar a pele de vocês."

am.L: አይቶም፦ «ሂዱ፤ ራሳችሁን ለካህናት አሳዩ» አላቸው።
am.B: ኢየሱስም አያቸውና «ሂዱ፤ ካህናቱ እንዲመረምሯችሁ ራሳችሁን አሳዩ» አላቸው።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ባያቸው ጊዜ «ሂዱ፤ ካህናቱ ቆዳችሁን እንዲያዩ አድርጉ» አላቸው።

decisions.choice: show yourselves to the priests: the step the law required before a cleansed person could return to the community
alternatives: a test of whether they were sick
decisions.reason: As at 5:14. A priest examined the skin and declared the person clean (Leviticus 14:1-32). Jesus sends them before they are healed, so going was an act of trust.

decisions.choice: let the priests examine you (B); let the priests look at your skin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:14, Balanced and Readable say why they were to go.

decisions.choice: "các anh" for the ten men
decisions.reason: As Jesus speaks to the blind men of Matthew 20:32: they are strangers who ask for help, not opponents.

decisions.choice: "몸을 보이고 검사를 받아라" (B); "피부를 보여라" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 5:14: the priests examined a healed person before he could return to the community (meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the going of them they were cleansed.

en.L: And it happened, as they went, [that] they were cleansed.
en.B: On their way there, they were made clean.
en.R: While they were going, they were healed and made clean.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras iban, fueron limpiados.
es.B: Mientras iban de camino, quedaron limpios.
es.R: Mientras iban, fueron sanados y quedaron limpios.

fr.L: Et il arriva, pendant qu’ils s’en allaient, [qu’]ils furent purifiés.
fr.B: En chemin, ils furent rendus purs.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils marchaient, ils ont été guéris, et ils sont devenus purs.

sw.L: Ikawa, walipokuwa wakienda, wakatakaswa.
sw.B: Walipokuwa njiani, walifanywa safi.
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakienda, waliponywa na kufanywa safi.

vi.L: Và xảy ra, trong khi họ đi, họ được sạch.
vi.B: Đang trên đường đi, họ được sạch.
vi.R: Trong khi họ đang đi, họ được lành bệnh và được sạch.

ko.L: 그리고 [이런] 일이 있었다. 그들이 가는 동안 깨끗하게 되었다.
ko.B: 그들은 가는 길에 깨끗해졌다.
ko.R: 그들이 가는 동안 병이 나아 깨끗해졌다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, enquanto iam, foram purificados.
pt.B: No caminho, eles ficaram limpos.
pt.R: Enquanto eles iam, foram curados e ficaram limpos.

am.L: ሲሄዱም እንዲህ ሆነ፤ ነጹ።
am.B: ወደዚያ በመሄድ ላይ ሳሉ ነጹ።
am.R: እየሄዱ ሳሉ ተፈወሱ፤ ነጹም።

decisions.choice: were cleansed: healed of the disease, and so made clean under the law
decisions.reason: As at 5:12-13, healing and being made clean go together.

decisions.choice: were cleansed: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who healed them unnamed; 17:15-18 shows that the healing came from God through Jesus.

decisions.choice: healed and made clean
decisions.reason: Readable says that being clean meant being healed.

source.text: εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη, ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Σαμαρίτης.

records.literal_gloss: One then of them, having seen that he was healed, turned back with a voice loud glorifying God, \v 16 and he fell on [his] face at the feet of him giving thanks to him; and he was a Samaritan.

en.L: And one of them, seeing that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice, \v 16 and he fell on [his] face at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, giving thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and he was a Samaritan.
en.B: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, giving glory to God with a loud voice. \v 16 He fell face down at the feet of Jesus, thanking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And the man was a Samaritan.
en.R: One of the men saw that he was healed. He came back, shouting and giving glory to God. \v 16 He bowed down at the feet of Jesus with his face to the ground and thanked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. This man was a Samaritan, not a Jew.

es.L: Y uno de ellos, al ver que había sido sanado, regresó glorificando a Dios a gran voz, \v 16 y cayó sobre [su] rostro a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, dándole gracias; y él era samaritano.
es.B: Uno de ellos, al ver que estaba sano, volvió dando gloria a Dios a gran voz. \v 16 Se postró rostro en tierra a los pies de Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio las gracias. Y ese hombre era samaritano.
es.R: Uno de los hombres vio que estaba sano. Regresó gritando y dando gloria a Dios. \v 16 Se inclinó a los pies de Jesús con la cara en el suelo y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio las gracias. Este hombre era samaritano, no judío.

fr.L: Or l’un d’eux, voyant qu’il était guéri, revint sur ses pas, glorifiant Dieu d’une voix forte, \v 16 et il tomba sur [sa] face à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendant grâce ; et c’était un Samaritain.
fr.B: L’un d’eux, quand il vit qu’il était guéri, revint sur ses pas en rendant gloire à Dieu d’une voix forte. \v 16 Il se jeta face contre terre aux pieds de Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} remercia. Or cet homme était un Samaritain.
fr.R: L’un des hommes a vu qu’il était guéri. Il est revenu en criant et en rendant gloire à Dieu. \v 16 Il s’est prosterné aux pieds de Jésus, le visage contre le sol, et il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a remercié. Cet homme était un Samaritain, il n’était pas juif.

sw.L: Na mmoja wao, alipoona kwamba ameponywa, alirudi akimtukuza Mungu kwa sauti kuu, \v 16 akaanguka kifudifudi miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}, akimshukuru; naye alikuwa Msamaria.
sw.B: Mmoja wao alipoona kwamba amepona, alirudi akimtukuza Mungu kwa sauti kubwa. \v 16 Alijitupa kifudifudi miguuni pa Yesu, akamshukuru. Mtu huyo alikuwa Msamaria.
sw.R: Mmoja wa wanaume hao aliona kwamba amepona. Alirudi akipiga kelele na kumtukuza Mungu. \v 16 Aliinama miguuni pa Yesu, uso wake ukigusa ardhi, akamshukuru. Mtu huyo alikuwa Msamaria, si Myahudi.

vi.L: Một người trong số họ, thấy mình được chữa lành, quay trở lại, lớn tiếng tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời, \v 16 và sấp mặt xuống dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; và người ấy là người Sa-ma-ri.
vi.B: Một người trong số họ, khi thấy mình được chữa lành, liền quay lại, lớn tiếng tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời. \v 16 Anh sấp mặt xuống dưới chân Đức Giê-xu mà cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Người ấy là một người Sa-ma-ri.
vi.R: Một người trong số họ thấy mình được lành bệnh. Anh quay trở lại, kêu lớn tiếng tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời. \v 16 Anh quỳ xuống, sấp mặt xuống đất dưới chân Đức Giê-xu và cảm tạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Người này là người Sa-ma-ri, không phải người Do Thái.

ko.L: 그런데 그들 가운데 하나가 자기가 나은 것을 보고 큰 소리로 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 돌아와서, \v 16 그분의 발 앞에 얼굴을 대고 엎드려 그분께 감사하였다. 그는 사마리아 사람이었다.
ko.B: 그들 가운데 한 사람은 자기 병이 나은 것을 보고, 큰 소리로 하나님께 영광을 돌리며 되돌아왔다. \v 16 그리고 예수의 발 앞에 엎드려 감사를 드렸다. 그 사람은 사마리아 사람이었다.
ko.R: 그들 가운데 한 사람은 자기 병이 나은 것을 알았다. 그는 큰 소리로 하나님을 찬양하며 되돌아왔다. \v 16 그리고 예수의 발 앞에 얼굴을 땅에 대고 엎드려 감사를 드렸다. 그는 유대 사람이 아니라 사마리아 사람이었다.

pt.L: E um deles, vendo que tinha sido curado, voltou, glorificando a Deus em alta voz, \v 16 e caiu com o rosto [em terra] aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés, dando-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} graças; e ele era samaritano.
pt.B: Um deles, quando viu que estava curado, voltou glorificando a Deus em alta voz. \v 16 Ele se prostrou com o rosto no chão aos pés de Jesus e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} agradeceu. E esse homem era samaritano.
pt.R: Um dos homens viu que estava curado. Ele voltou gritando e dando glória a Deus. \v 16 Ele se ajoelhou aos pés de Jesus com o rosto no chão e agradeceu a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Esse homem era samaritano, não judeu.

am.L: ከእነርሱም አንዱ እንደ ተፈወሰ ባየ ጊዜ በታላቅ ድምፅ እግዚአብሔርን እያከበረ ተመለሰ፤ \v 16 በእግሩም ሥር በግንባሩ ተደፍቶ አመሰገነው፤ እርሱም ሳምራዊ ነበረ።
am.B: ከእነርሱ አንዱ እንደ ተፈወሰ ባየ ጊዜ በታላቅ ድምፅ እግዚአብሔርን እያከበረ ተመለሰ። \v 16 በኢየሱስ እግር ሥር በግንባሩ ተደፍቶ አመሰገነው። ሰውየውም ሳምራዊ ነበረ።
am.R: ከሰዎቹ አንዱ እንደ ተፈወሰ አየ። እየጮኸና እግዚአብሔርን እያከበረ ተመለሰ። \v 16 በኢየሱስ እግር ሥር በግንባሩ ተደፍቶ አመሰገነው። ይህ ሰው አይሁዳዊ ሳይሆን ሳምራዊ ነበረ።

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he had done
decisions.reason: As in 5:25 and 7:16, the healed man honors God aloud for the healing.

decisions.choice: Samaritan: one of the people of Samaria, despised by many Jews
alternatives: a man from the city of Samaria only
decisions.reason: Jews and Samaritans had a long history of hostility over worship and descent (9:52-53; John 4:9). Like the Samaritan in Jesus' story (10:33), it is the outsider who does what is right.

decisions.choice: fell on his face: bowed with his face to the ground
decisions.reason: A gesture of deep honor and thanks (5:12).

decisions.choice: the feet of Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since "his" could refer to the man.

decisions.choice: not a Jew
decisions.reason: Readable adds what made this man different from the others, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "하나님께 영광을 돌리다" (L, B), "하나님을 찬양하다" (R); "사마리아 사람"
decisions.reason: Glory is a key term, kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what the giving of glory was (meaning decision). "사마리아 사람" as the style guide and the Korean Luke 10:33.

decisions.choice: በግንባሩ ተደፍቶ (prostrated with his forehead to the ground)
decisions.reason: "በግንባር መደፋት" is the Amharic way of saying that someone bowed with his face to the ground, which is the sense (m3).

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν;

records.literal_gloss: Having answered then Jesus said, Not the ten were cleansed?

en.L: And Jesus answered and said, "Were not the ten cleansed?
en.B: Jesus responded, "Ten men were made clean, were they not?
en.R: Jesus asked, "Did not all ten men become clean?

es.L: Y respondiendo Jesús, dijo: «¿No fueron limpiados los diez?
es.B: Jesús respondió: «Diez hombres quedaron limpios, ¿no es así?
es.R: Jesús preguntó: «¿No quedaron limpios los diez?

fr.L: Et Jésus, répondant, dit : « Les dix n’ont-ils pas été purifiés ?
fr.B: Jésus prit la parole : « Dix hommes ont été rendus purs, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Jésus a demandé : « Les dix hommes ne sont-ils pas tous devenus purs ?

sw.L: Naye Yesu akajibu, akasema, "Je, wale kumi hawakutakaswa?
sw.B: Yesu alijibu, "Watu kumi walifanywa safi, sivyo?
sw.R: Yesu aliuliza, "Je, wanaume wote kumi hawakufanywa safi?

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp lời mà nói: "Chẳng phải cả mười người đều được sạch sao?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Có mười người được sạch, phải không?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi: "Chẳng phải cả mười người đều được sạch sao?

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "열 사람이 깨끗하게 되지 않았느냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "깨끗해진 사람은 열 명이 아니었느냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 물으셨다. "열 사람이 다 깨끗해지지 않았느냐?

pt.L: E Jesus, respondendo, disse: "Não foram purificados os dez?
pt.B: Jesus respondeu: "Os dez homens ficaram limpos, não ficaram?
pt.R: Jesus perguntou: "Os dez homens não ficaram todos limpos?

am.L: ኢየሱስም መልሶ እንዲህ አለ፦ «አሥሩ አልነጹምን?
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አለ፦ «የነጹት አሥር ሰዎች አልነበሩምን?
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ብሎ ጠየቀ፦ «አሥሩም ሰዎች አልነጹምን?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "yes"
alternatives: a real question asking for information
decisions.reason: Jesus knows that all ten were cleansed. The question points to the one who came back.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:18
decisions.reason: Jesus' three questions are one speech.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;

records.literal_gloss: But the nine, where?

en.L: But the nine, where [are they]?
en.B: So where are the other nine?
en.R: Where are the other nine men?

es.L: ¿Y los nueve, dónde [están]?
